Elena / Mina — sharing a concise technical summary to accompany the diagrams and runbook. This is meant to be included verbatim in the mapping pack if helpful.

Summary (technical highlights):
- Control plane vs data plane:
  - Control plane (scheduler, model registry, routing) is hosted in Redwood-managed VPCs and uses private peering/internal APIs. Customers do not have direct network access to control plane hosts. Access to management APIs is authenticated/authorized and logged.
  - Data plane (model inference execution) differs by deployment:
    - Hosted / Dedicated: data-plane runs on dedicated GPU pools isolated by tenant; no customer VPC peering by default — connectivity flows outbound to customer endpoints when configured (egress) or responses are returned via Redwood API.
    - Private (VPC): data plane can be deployed into a customer-managed VPC via one of the following stitching patterns: VPC peering (same region), Transit Gateway, or site-to-site VPN/Direct Connect for high-throughput requirements. For on-prem air-gapped installs we ship a hardened appliance with explicit ingress rules and an offline attestation flow.
- Tenant fencing and host isolation: per-tenant namespaces, container-level runtime isolation, ephemeral worker pools, and strict OCI image signing policies. KV caches are tenant-scoped and not persisted to shared customer volumes.
- KMS / key boundary: Customer-managed keys (CMK) supported via KMS integration (Bring Your Own Key). For Private deployments keys may be provided from customer KMS/HSM and are never exported.
- Egress, DNS, and flow controls: configurable egress whitelists, egress proxies, and mandatory TLS 1.2+ for all external flows. For Dedicated we recommend egress NAT with customer-applied firewall rules; for Private we can honor customer routing and security groups.
- Observability / evidence: flow logs, VPC flow capture, and audit logs can be provided as redacted extracts for SOC2 review. We keep per-request tracing metadata for 90 days by default (configurable).

Attached: private-onprem-deployment-runbook-v1.2.pdf (contains appliance network diagrams, port lists, and hardening checklist).

If you want, we can add an appendix that maps each diagram element to specific SIG/CAIQ control IDs.

—Karthik
Director, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
